headline: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches for critical 9.2/10 severity vulnerabilities
summary: The patches address two vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 out of 10 severity, with security firms expecting mass attacks within minutes of release.
details: PHP maintainers have announced emergency patches for two critical vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 out of 10 severity. All PHP users are urged to prepare for immediate upgrade, with patches expected within 12 hours but potentially earlier if details leak or active exploitation begins.

An unconfirmed report detailed a PHP2Shell exploit tool, reportedly capable of executing code remotely on various popular web platforms. This includes WordPress, MediaWiki, Magento, Joomla, and Drupal, affecting all PHP versions from PHP 5 (released in 2004) onwards.

Security firms watchTowr, Sansec, Webfence, and Huntress have confirmed the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Sansec specifically warned that "mass attacks are expected to start within 15 minutes of the release."

Preparation steps include identifying PHP managers, inventorying all apps built on the language, and planning a maintenance window starting at 14:00 UTC. Admins should also back up site and database files, and monitor the PHP.net homepage for any late-breaking announcements or earlier release times.

Given that PHP powers an estimated 1.3 million internet-connected hosts, these high-severity vulnerabilities have the potential to inflict major damage across the internet. Some experts suggest unplugging any non-essential systems until they are patched, and admins must remain vigilant as patches could drop at any moment.
